title: capture_signup_lead hands a fresh claim token to anyone who submits an address already in signup_leads, letting a stranger take over that lead row.

source.ref: SCAN-1224 review of the anon-callable SECURITY DEFINER functions, 2026-11-16 (security thread, requested by Daniel). Confidence: PLAUSIBLE (read from the live function body; not exercised).

detail:
EVIDENCE: public.capture_signup_lead(...) upserts on lower(email) and, on conflict, sets claim_token_hash = excluded.claim_token_hash and returns the new raw token (its header says the most recent browser to give the address holds the row, by design). update_signup_lead then accepts that token. So anyone who knows an address can rotate the token, lock the real person's browser out of its own lead row, and overwrite the row's names, handle and payload (a new answer wins).

WHY IT MATTERS: The row is marketing lead data, not an account, so reach is small: a victim's funnel progress and saved Space draft can be overwritten or disconnected by a stranger who only knows their email. Anything that later trusts the row's payload as the person's own answer should treat it as unverified.

FIX DIRECTION: Keep the first token for an existing address and return a not-yours answer to later callers, or require the email to be confirmed (magic link) before a token is rotated; at minimum stop a later submission from overwriting names, handle and payload that already exist. Ships as a migration through the gated path.

verify.evidence: Open: a second capture_signup_lead call for the same address still rotates claim_token_hash. Close when a repeat call cannot take the row from the first holder.
